relevance_note: Case report of two sisters with SSADH deficiency homozygous for an ALDH5A1 variant: 'DNA sequence analysis demonstrated a homozygous mutation in the ALDH5A1 gene (c.1226G>A; p.Gly409Asp)'.
method_note: Hand-read the whole paper (no tables); a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON. Labels: the paper uses only role words ('the proband', 'the decedent'), so the proband is 'patient' (rule 5) and her deceased older sister 'sister of patient' (rule 2); the two parents ('Both parents were tested and confirmed as heterozygous') are in scope as tested relatives, sex not stated, labelled 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2'. Inheritance for both daughters recorded as 'inherited unspecified parent' because both parents (sex not given) are stated to be heterozygous carriers of the same variant; no maternal/paternal enum fits a homozygote. Parents' pathogenicity and functional evidence left 'not reported' (D-29: about the proband's variant). Consanguinity is stated in the proband's paragraph only; left 'not reported' for the sister, although Figure 1 says both parents' results confirm homozygosity 'in both children'. Ethnicity: proband's parents 'of Greek ancestry'; the abstract calls the decedent 'of European origin'. Normal findings (D-27): 'satisfactory strength' -> muscle weakness excluded; 'response to the Romberg test was normal' -> abnormal Romberg excluded; EEGs 'unremarkable' -> abnormal EEG excluded; 'ventricular system was normal in size and configuration' recorded as written. 'No detected systemic or toxicologic abnormalities' and 'no gross neuropathologic findings, except for leptomeningeal congestion' are whole-examination statements; recorded only as written (the former), nothing more specific excluded (cerebral atrophy left not reported). 'Absence of tremor or dyskinesias' on examination was not used to exclude the checklist item 'exertional dyskinesia'; wide-based gait was not taken as ataxia. Contradictions: (1) Figure 2D legend reports 'Granular perivascular calcification in putamen' while the text says 'No other changes were evident in the other deep cerebral nuclei, including the caudate, putamen' and lists calcifications only in globus pallidus, dentate nucleus and hippocampus; both rows emitted. (2) Timing: the abstract says the decedent died in 1998 and the sister presented 'Eight years later', whereas the case report says the sister 'died 6 years earlier'; no age field depends on this. Age at diagnosis for the proband taken from the abstract ('presented at 13 years of age with seizures and was diagnosed'); the decedent's diagnosis was posthumous ('10 years after her death'), no age given.
